```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 9,
  fig.height = 8
)
```

```{r setup}
library(golfops)
sample <- dobson_operating_daily()
played <- sample[!is.na(sample$rounds_played) & sample$rounds_played > 0, ]
categories <- c(
  "Total revenue" = "total_revenue",
  "Green fees" = "green_fee_revenue",
  "Food and beverage" = "food_beverage_revenue",
  "Merchandise" = "merchandise_revenue",
  "Range" = "range_revenue",
  "Cart" = "cart_revenue",
  "Club rental" = "club_revenue"
)
revenue_correlation <- function(block) {
  round(vapply(categories, function(column) {
    stats::cor(block$rounds_played, block[[column]], use = "complete.obs")
  }, numeric(1)), 2)
}
```

```{r correlation-table, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
years <- 2021:2026
correlation_table <- sapply(years, function(year) {
  revenue_correlation(played[played$calendar_year == year, ])
})
colnames(correlation_table) <- c("2021*", "2022", "2023", "2024", "2025", "2026*")
knitr::kable(
  correlation_table,
  caption = "Correlation of golfers with each daily revenue amount. * 2021 and 2026 are half years: 2021 is July through December, and 2026 is January through April."
)
```

## Annual revenue

Each chart is one revenue type. The horizontal axis is the year, and the bar is that year's revenue. Total revenue is the last chart. Pale bars are half years: 2021 is July through December, and 2026 is January through April.

```{r annual, fig.width = 7.2, fig.height = 12, fig.alt = "Seven bar charts of annual revenue, one revenue type each, with total revenue last. 2021 and 2026 are marked as half years."}
plot_annual_revenue(sample)
```

The city file records daily total revenue, green fees, food and beverage, merchandise, range, cart rental, and club rental, along with golfers, from 2021-07-01 through the latest day in the extract. Food and beverage is one amount. Dining is not split from alcohol.

Mesa's annual comprehensive financial report does not publish that split for Dobson Ranch either. The course's restaurant and shop are run by a concessionaire. The daily open-data file is the source for these categories.

Each section is one calendar year. Each point is one day with at least one golfer. The horizontal axis is golfers. The line in each panel is a straight fit to that year's days. 2021 starts on July 1, and the latest year ends with the extract.

## 2021

```{r year-2021, fig.alt = "2021 daily revenue against golfers, seven panels, from July 1."}
plot_revenue_by_golfers(sample, year = 2021)
```


These are associations in the recorded days. They are not evidence that an extra golfer causes the extra spending, and they are not a price.
